about: Powers the 💰 Best Sellers tab: scoring weights for what actually moves, plus the channel matrix for auctions, live selling, and YouTube. Figures marked (est.) are compiled from public hobby sources and change often — always confirm against live sold comps.

scoring.note: score = value × band × eraHeat × setHeat × langFactor (+ graded bonus). Tuned for LIQUIDITY — how fast a card sells at asking — not just raw value.

priceBands.label: Bulk zone
priceBands.advice: Don't list singly — feed these into lots, repacks, and Brand Lab packaging. Fees eat singles under $10.

priceBands.label: Slow singles
priceBands.advice: Sell in themed 3–5 card lots or live streams; single listings sit.

priceBands.label: Sweet spot
priceBands.advice: Fastest-moving band on eBay & Whatnot — impulse-buyable, comps are tight. (est.)

priceBands.label: Serious buyers
priceBands.advice: Strong demand; buyers expect crisp photos and exact condition notes.

priceBands.label: Big tickets
priceBands.advice: Fewer buyers, slower — but auctions with a modest start price find true market. Consider grading first.

setHeat.why: Scarlet & Violet 151 nostalgia demand keeps sell-through high. (est.)
2025 Team Rocket revival sets run hot. (est.)
Promos vary wildly — comp each one individually.

channels.name: eBay Auctions (bidding)
channels.bestFor: True price discovery on $100+ cards, hyped modern hits, graded slabs
channels.avoid: Sub-$25 cards (fees + low bids), anything you have a firm floor on
tips: Start at $0.99 ONLY for cards with proven comp depth; otherwise start at ~70% of recent solds
7-day auction ending Sunday 6–9pm Pacific catches both US coasts (est.)
Batch 5–10 auctions ending the same night — bidders cross-shop your other lots
Use all 24 photo slots; the Scanner tab's saved shots drop straight in

channels.name: eBay Buy-It-Now
channels.bestFor: Sweet-spot singles ($25–$400) priced at comp, Best Offer on
channels.avoid: Rare low-pop cards where you'd leave auction upside on the table
tips: Price at the last 3 solds' median, enable offers, auto-decline below 85%
Promoted listings at 2% is usually worth it for visibility (est.)
Refresh stale listings every 30 days — sell-similar re-indexes you

channels.name: Whatnot Live (live + bidding)
channels.bestFor: Moving VOLUME — bulk lots, $10–$100 singles, repacks, building a following
channels.avoid: Your top 5 cards until your stream has regulars bidding them up
tips: Apply as a seller first (approval takes days); category: Trading Card Games
Sudden-death auctions at $1 start move 60–100 lots in a 2-hour show (est.)
Schedule the same night weekly — repeat viewers are 80% of live sales (est.)
Point a second camera at a Den-style display shelf behind you — set dressing sells

channels.name: YouTube (channel + live)
channels.bestFor: Brand building: collection tours, top-10s, grading reveals, den tours; drives buyers to your streams and listings
channels.avoid: Selling in comments/DMs — scams; always route to a real marketplace
tips: Shorts of single-card showcases (the 3D Studio spin view screen-records beautifully)
PSA return reveal videos are the highest-retention card format (est.)
Link your eBay store + Whatnot schedule in every description
YouTube Live 'rip and ship' requires routing sales through a marketplace — Whatnot or eBay Live handles compliance for you

channels.name: Facebook Marketplace (local)
channels.bestFor: Zero-fee local deals, bulk lots, meetups at card shops
channels.avoid: Shipping to strangers — local pickup only unless buyer pays G&S
tips: Meet at a card shop or police-station exchange zone, daytime
Bundle bulk into $20/$50/$100 mystery boxes for parents — fastest local mover
Cross-post to local Pokémon TCG Facebook groups the same day

channels.name: TCGplayer
channels.bestFor: Near-mint EN singles $2–$50 at scale — set-and-forget inventory
channels.avoid: Japanese cards (thin market there) and heavy-played condition disputes
tips: Condition honestly — TCGplayer buyers refund aggressively on NM claims

channels.name: Mercari
channels.bestFor: Mid-range singles and small lots; casual buyers pay closer to ask
channels.avoid: High-value cards — buyer protection disputes favor buyers (est.)
tips: 'Smart pricing' floor at your real floor; let it drip down to sell

auctionNight.title: Auction Night playbook (bidding, done right)
steps: Pick 8–12 cards from the Best-Sell board below — mix one anchor ($150+), five sweet-spot, and a few lots
Shoot every card in 📷 Scanner first — front, back, corners; photos auto-attach to the card file
List all as 7-day auctions ending the same Sunday evening, 2 minutes apart
Share the auction batch link to your YouTube community tab + FB groups on Thursday
Ship Monday in one batch run; save tracking against each card's note

livePlaybook.title: Going live (Whatnot / eBay Live / YouTube)
steps: Apply for Whatnot seller status now — approval lead time is the bottleneck
Build a backdrop: Den-style shelf, ring light, phone on the GradeStage rig
First 3 shows: $1-start bulk + sweet-spot singles to build ratings; no anchors
Announce a recurring slot (e.g. 'Chest Night — Thursdays 7pm MT')
Stream the show simultaneously to YouTube for discovery; sales stay on Whatnot

notes: Fees above are headline rates (est.) — category promos and store subscriptions change them.
Every venue's real net for a specific card is in that card's sell panel — this tab is for choosing WHAT to sell and WHERE.
Not financial advice. Check live sold comps before committing an anchor card.
